entry.title: Thermal Krylov complexity and entropy of inflationary modes with different comoving-wavenumber dependences
entry.summary: We study thermal Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy for primordial scalar modes in three inflationary models with different comoving-wavenumber dependences. These models are canonical single-field inflation, a non-trivial sound speed model, and a modified dispersion relation model. We construct a purified two-mode thermal state and first study its unitary Krylov evolution in an ideal closed system. In the parameter range considered here, the sound-speed correction increases the mean values and oscillation amplitudes of the Krylov quantities. The modified dispersion relation produces a stage-dependent oscillatory structure. We then introduce an independent effective open-system parametrization. The normalized Krylov distribution is controlled by a geometric ratio that combines thermal occupation, coherent spreading, and effective attenuation. We derive explicit expressions for Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy. We also obtain their low- and high-temperature limits. The sound-speed correction enhances the geometric ratio in the adopted parameter range. For the modified dispersion relation, coherent spreading and effective attenuation compete. These results show how thermal occupation and modified mode frequencies control Krylov-space spreading in the three inflationary models.

entry.title: Dipolar Exchange and Emergent Electric-Dipole-Carrying Quasiparticles in Electronic Ferroelectrics
entry.summary: Electronic correlations underpin diverse spontaneously ordered states in matter, whose collective excitations emerge as quasiparticles that encode the underlying order. While spin exchange interactions give rise to magnetic order and its quasiparticle excitations known as magnons, their counterparts in electronic ferroelectrics remain poorly understood. Here, we derive an analogous quantum dipolar-pseudospin exchange model for electronic ferroelectricity and identify the associated bosonic quasiparticles that carry intrinsic electric dipole moments. Unlike ferrons in conventional lattice-based ferroelectrics, these dipolar quasiparticles arise entirely from collective electronic dynamics without involving lattice vibrations. Their excitation spectrum exhibits a linear Stark shift under a static electric field, while coupling to an oscillating electric field enables their coherent excitation, leading to colossal, resonantly enhanced second-harmonic generation and optical rectification in the terahertz regime. These dipolar quasiparticles offer promising opportunities for electrically tunable nonlinear optics and open a route toward extending the paradigm of transport in electronic systems beyond conventional charge currents to electric dipole currents.

entry.title: Quartet ferromagnetism in the small-exchange limit
entry.summary: Rare-earth magnets are often regarded as classical owing to their large angular momentum J, but this picture breaks down when exchange is smaller than the crystalline electric-field (CEF) energy scale, allowing the degeneracy of low-lying CEF manifolds to dictate the emergent quantum phases. Here, we uncover such a regime in the RV6Sn6 (R = rare-earth) kagome metals with strong magnetic anisotropy. Thermodynamic and neutron-diffraction measurements reveal successive axial and tilted ferromagnetic (FM) phases in DyV6Sn6, arising from independent ordering of the axial Mz and transverse Mx dipolar components enabled by a rare quasi-quartet ground state. On the other hand, HoV6Sn6 has a similar tilted magnetic anisotropy, but remains axial down to 0.03 K. This discrepancy can be traced back to the non-Kramers nature of Ho3+ where the CEF lifts the quartet degeneracy, leaving a quasi-triplet ground state. Unlike quartets or higher multiplets, we find that the effective spin-1 triplet does not allow independent dipolar ordering without strong quadrupolar (nematic) interactions that act to break rotational symmetry, revealing an essential multipolar prerequisite for tilted magnetic ground states. These results establish a quartet CEF manifold as the minimal degeneracy required for dipolar-driven independent ordering. Mapping the surrounding CEF parameter space further reveals competing magnetic, non-magnetic singlet, and potential quadrupolar phases, driven by multifold ground state degeneracies. These results establish CEF tuning as a versatile route to unconventional quantum phases across the broader RT6X6 (T = transition metal; X = Sn, Ge) family.

entry.title: Thouless pumping and Haldane-model topology in a driven extended SSH chain
entry.summary: Thouless pumping provides a powerful route for probing Chern topology through quantized motion in one-dimensional lattices. We investigate such a topological pump in an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model with tunable next-nearest-neighbor hoppings. A graphical representation in Bloch space is used to construct pumping schemes. In this framework, the Bloch vector traces a closed loop that evolves in time. The Chern number of the synthetic band is then determined by the motion of this loop. Quantum pumping phenomena are demonstrated for a filled band and for a bosonic wave packet driven by Bloch oscillations. We further show that the Haldane model can be mapped to the driven extended SSH chain by replacing a quasimomentum by the pumping time. The quantized charge pump indicates that the Chern number of a two-dimensional model can be read out from a one-dimensional pumping protocol, offering an accessible route for detecting higher-dimensional topology, such as in photonic and cold-atom platforms.

entry.title: Non-Relativistic Supersymmetric Gauge Theories and Soliton Solutions
entry.summary: This paper investigates non-relativistic supersymmetric gauge theories obtained through null reduction, with particular focus on supersymmetric Abelian Higgs models and their soliton solutions. Starting from four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 1$ relativistic supersymmetric theories, we apply null reduction to derive Galilean-invariant non-relativistic theories in $2 + 1$ dimensions while preserving gauge symmetry and supersymmetry. The resulting symmetry structure is shown to correspond to the Bargmann extension of the super-Galilean algebra. We first analyze the massive supersymmetric Abelian Higgs model and show that, although it possesses nontrivial vacuum configurations, the mass term obstructs the existence of nontrivial BPS vortex solutions. We then study the massless supersymmetric Abelian Higgs model with multiple charged scalar fields, for which the BPS equations admit vortex-type soliton solutions under suitable charge and winding number conditions. The vacuum moduli space is identified as a weighted projective space, leading naturally to both integer and fractional vortex configurations. By imposing radial symmetry, we derive the corresponding vortex equations and examine their solutions analytically and numerically. Finally, we relate the vacuum structure of the model to the Ginzburg-Landau theory of superconductivity, highlighting how familiar superconducting behavior can emerge from a symmetry-preserving non-relativistic supersymmetric framework.

entry.title: Pseudogap in hole doped cuprates: a status report
entry.summary: The pseudogap state, an anomalous momentum dependent partial suppression of low energy electronic excitations persisting well above the superconducting critical temperature in underdoped cuprates, remains one of the most profound enigmas in condensed physics today. This review summarizes over three decades of experimental and theoretical progress. It appears that pseudogap is not a mere precursor to superconductivity, but a distinct, intertwined state of matter characterized by a complex interplay of competing and cooperating electronic orders. We critically examine the bulk probes like resistivity and magnetic susceptibility and the surface hallmark spectroscopic signatures observed via angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) in this review. ARPES reveals a Fermi surface truncated into disconnected segments and scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) visualizes a spatially heterogeneous energy gap around the Fermi level. These observations are contextualized alongside transport anomalies, including resistivity and bulk magnetic susceptibility, to construct a phenomenological portrait of a phase that violates conventional Fermi liquid theory. By mapping the electronic phase diagram, we highlight the abrupt transition at above optimal doping. We conclude with open questions still to be answered. This review underscores the role of the pseudogap as a key to unlocking the unconventional pairing mechanism of hole doped cuprates and the broader physics of strongly correlated electron systems.

entry.title: Transverse quasiparticle heat transport in p-wave magnetic Josephson junctions
entry.summary: We study transverse heat currents carried by Bogoliubov quasiparticles in $p$-wave magnetic Josephson junctions under a longitudinal temperature bias. We find that such a junction supports a transverse spin heat current while the net transverse heat current vanishes. This effect stems from the $p$-wave magnetism, which shifts the two spin sectors oppositely in transverse momentum space and thereby causes them to carry opposite heat currents. A weak Zeeman field lifts the compensation between the two spin-sector contributions, thereby generating a finite net transverse heat current. The directions of both currents can be switched by reversing the sign of the $p$-wave magnetic splitting or tuning the superconducting phase difference, while both currents vanish in the absence of $p$-wave magnetism. These findings highlight $p$-wave magnetic Josephson junctions as a versatile platform for switchable transverse heat transport and controllable spin caloritronics.

entry.title: Faint Thermonuclear Transients from the Double Detonations of Common White Dwarfs
entry.summary: The double detonation model is a viable channel to explain many observed Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), with thin helium shelled white dwarf (WD) progenitors of 0.9--1.1 M$_\odot$ reproducing normal SNe Ia observables. Recent work has also shown that all C/O WDs $\leq$ 1.0 M$_\odot$ can sustain a helium shell detonation that triggers a detonation of the underlying core. As WDs of lower masses (0.5--0.7 M$_\odot$) far outnumber those at higher mass, it is important to explore their double detonation outcomes. To that end, we conducted multidimensional double detonation simulations of low mass C/O cores with very thin helium shells, finding explosion outcomes that differ non-trivially from those at higher masses. Not surprisingly, their cores are incompletely burned with low yields of radioactive elements. Though still formally unbound in isolation, some of the ejecta could remain bound to a nearby companion. In addition, the offset initiation of the core detonation wave and its failure to burn through the entire core lead to a very asymmetric distribution of $^{56}$Ni that creates dramatically viewing angle-dependent light curves and spectra. We find that the peak bolometric luminosities for the same explosion vary up to nearly 2 magnitudes over the sky, and that the spectra and light curves from these models are within the range of faint SNe Iax. In particular, our 0.50 M$_\odot$ models agree well with the photometry of SNe Iax 2008ha and 2024vjm.

entry.title: Current Closure and Gamma-Ray Signatures of Spark-Gap and Current-Sheet Activities in Radiative Black Hole Magnetospheres
entry.summary: We investigate the evolution of an axisymmetric black hole magnetosphere using general relativistic particle-in-cell simulations, focusing on its global current structure, variability, and radiative effects. We include inverse-Compton (IC) scattering of ambient photons and subsequent two-photon pair production, and compare simulations with and without synchrotron-curvature (SC) radiation reaction. Starting from an axisymmetric vertical magnetic field, the system develops a polar spark gap and a variable equatorial current sheet that together sustain the global poloidal current. For the parameters explored in this study, we observe that the spark gap oscillates upon the onset of SC cooling, whereas the current sheet is less sensitive to radiative cooling. Time-dependent electric fields in the return-current layer trigger magnetic-field rearrangement followed by magnetic reconnection. Cross-correlation analysis finds no significant correlation between the two regions' variability, suggesting dynamical independence. We further perform post-processing ray-tracing calculations to evaluate the radiative efficiencies of the IC and SC processes. High-energy particles dominate the bolometric luminosity, which reaches up to 1 percent of the Blandford-Znajek luminosity for SC emission and 0.1 percent for IC emission. The relative IC luminosity to SC is higher at lower viewing angles because particle momenta are more anisotropic near the pole than near the equator, due to efficient acceleration along the local magnetic field lines. Together with energetic estimates, these results suggest that both regions can contribute to high-energy emission in active galactic nuclei, with spark-gap photons reaching the sub-TeV regime.

entry.title: Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
entry.summary: The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions whose bulk dual is not yet identified, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. We show that the $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and analytically compute their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.

entry.title: Momentum-Resolved Kondo Hybridization of Nonsymmorphic Dirac-Derived Bands in CeAgBi$_2$
entry.summary: How symmetry-constrained conduction states acquire heavy-quasiparticle character is a central question in correlated quantum materials. Combining angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, Ce $4d \rightarrow 4f$ resonant photoemission, and first-principles calculations, we investigate the nonsymmorphic Kondo lattice CeAgBi$_2$. We identify quasi-two-dimensional Bi-square-net-derived bands consistent with calculated Dirac crossings and nodal lines. Resonant photoemission resolves a nearly dispersionless Ce 4$f$ band near the Fermi level, establishing Kondo heavy-quasiparticle states. Its pronounced momentum-dependent spectral weight at intersections with the identified Dirac-derived branches provides direct spectroscopic evidence for their participation in $c$-$f$ hybridization. Complementary measurements on independently cleaved samples and an effective hybridization model connect these branches to the Kondo heavy-quasiparticle spectrum. The combined results support preservation of nonsymmorphic Dirac-band connectivity under Kondo renormalization, showing how symmetry-constrained conduction states become constituents of correlated heavy quasiparticles.

entry.title: Self-correcting qubit in a strongly driven LC resonator
entry.summary: We propose a device to realize quantum error correction by dissipation. The device generates Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states as steady states in a single driven LC resonator. The resonator should have impedance above $h/2e^2\approx 12.9\,{\rm k}Ω$, and should be driven across a Josephson junction with a high-amplitude voltage tone at frequency near-commensurate with the resonator frequency. In this regime, we show that GKP states emerge as steady-states of the resonator; these states encode a qubit protected against phase-space local noise. Low-lying excitations preserve the quantum information and increase the energy proportionally to a measure of the error degree. Thus, quantum error correction of both bit and phase errors can be achieved with dissipative cooling. Our calculations indicate an achievable coherence time of $ 1000 \times$ the resonator photon lifetime at operating temperatures above $100 \, {\rm mK}$. Beyond steady-state quantum error correction, the device supports protected single-qubit Clifford gates and readout with exponential accuracy corrected by the same dissipative mechanism, as well as magic-state preparation above the distillation threshold.

entry.title: Discovery of Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line Topological State in strongly correlated material CeAuAl$_3$
entry.summary: Kramers nodal lines (KNLs) are predicted in all achiral, non-centrosymmetric crystal structures, and yet there are very few experimental realizations of KNLs, only in weakly correlated systems. Especially, their realization in strongly correlated systems remains unexplored. Here we investigate KNL topology in the non-centrosymmetric, achiral Kondo lattice CeAuAl$_3$, using magnetotransport, thermodynamic measurements, density functional theory (DFT), and tight-binding toy model calculations. We find that CeAuAl$_3$ hosts KNLs in the $\mathitΓ\text{-}Z$ and $X\text{-}P$ directions, protected by time-reversal and mirror symmetries. Breaking of these crystalline symmetries, along with time-reversal symmetry via spin polarization, lifts the KNL degeneracy, which, in turn, generates Berry curvature resulting in an intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE). More importantly, CeAuAl$_3$ shows large AHE not only below the magnetic ordering temperature $T_N$ but rather below the Kondo temperature. This underscores the role of the Kondo correlations in bringing the KNLs at the Fermi surface rather than at accidental energies, as would be expected without correlations. Our work identifies a new topological state, Kondo-Kramers Nodal Line, with CeAuAl$_3$ being the first compound explicitly identified to host this new correlated topological state, and demonstrating the expected AHE associated with it. More generally, our work outlines the pathway for finding Kondo-KNL systems in all compounds that combine achiral, non-centrosymmetric structure with Kondo correlations.

entry.title: Dimensional dependence of critical phenomena in black hole interiors
entry.summary: Black hole interiors exhibit a critical transition in which a perturbed inner horizon either survives or collapses into a spacelike singularity, but whether the exponent governing this transition depends on spacetime dimension has remained an open question. In this paper, we numerically investigate the interior dynamics of $D$ dimensional Reissner-Nordström (RN) black holes perturbed by a real scalar field. Strong perturbations destroy the null inner horizon and produce a spacelike singularity, whereas weaker perturbations preserve it with an areal radius that decreases as the perturbation amplitude increases. As the initial scalar field amplitude $p$ approaches its critical value $p^{*}$, the inner horizon radius decreases continuously to zero. Near criticality, this radius obeys the power law $r_{s}\propto|p-p^{*}|^γ$. In four dimensions, different initial scalar field profiles and initial RN black hole charges yield nearly identical critical exponents, $γ\simeq1/2$, supporting the universality of the scaling law. Within the investigated range $4\leq D\leq9$, the critical exponent decreases systematically with increasing spacetime dimension. The numerical results suggest the scaling relation $r_s\propto|p-p^{*}|^{1/(D-2)}$. This result establishes a new dimension-dependent universality class for interior black hole critical phenomena, distinct from the standard Choptuik collapse scaling.

entry.title: An RG perspective on the (un)naturalness of Starobinsky inflation
entry.summary: Starobinsky inflation is often regarded as a successful minimal model of the early universe, yet it relies on a large $R^2$-coupling, in apparent tension with the expectation that Wilson coefficients in a gravitational effective field theory are of the same order. We test this expectation with a first-principles renormalization group calculation. We use asymptotically safe gravity as a testing ground to define ultraviolet-complete renormalization group trajectories and to uniquely predict higher-order couplings in terms of the free parameters of the theory---the cosmological constant and the $R^2$-coupling in Planck units. Including higher-curvature operators up to the fourth order, we find that indeed the flow generates dimensionless couplings of comparable size in the ultraviolet, with the irrelevant couplings tied to the relevant ones by linear relations. However, at sub-Planckian energies a canonical-like scaling takes over, and the irrelevant couplings get suppressed by powers of the ratio between the inflationary and Planck scales. This hierarchy yields the suppression of higher-order operators needed for consistency with cosmological data, so that the $R^2$-dominated dynamics emerges as a natural low-energy approximation. At the same time, the higher-order terms required by fundamental physics induce small but calculable deviations from the Starobinsky predictions, which may be worth considering in light of the latest and future DESI and ACT results.

entry.title: Transient discs around isolated accreting neutron stars
entry.summary: Mature, isolated neutron stars can accrete from the interstellar medium. Due to turbulence, the accreted gas can have a substantial angular momentum and form a disc around the compact object. In this paper, we perform a population synthesis of isolated neutron stars in the Milky Way that specifically tracks the possibility of disc formation, which typically requires a low spatial velocity of the compact object ($\lesssim 40$ km s$^{-1}$). In general, weak magnetic fields favour disc formation as the magnetosphere occupies a smaller volume. Still, even in the case of fields decaying exponentially over a characteristic timescale of $\sim 1.5$ Gyr, we find that for several realistic models of propeller spin-down, only a small fraction of accretors (down to $\sim 0.02$ %) attain discs. However, disc-accreting isolated neutron stars are relatively numerous among the brightest sources. We estimate that their number can reach a few hundred at X-ray fluxes of $\gtrsim 10^{-14}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$. We speculate that disc-accreting isolated neutron stars can manifest as long-period radio transient sources via electron cyclotron maser emission, predicting spectra and critical conditions for quenching.

entry.title: Relativistic Simulations of Self-Gravitating Radiation Fluids
entry.summary: We present an approach for numerical simulations of pure radiation fluids within the general relativistic hydrodynamics framework. The approach models radiation as a self-gravitating perfect fluid with vanishing rest mass, enabling simulations of radiation fluids in strong-gravity spacetimes. Building on the existing relativistic hydrodynamics code Whisky, within the Einstein Toolkit framework, we introduce modifications to incorporate radiation fluids, including updates to the source terms, recovery scheme, and Riemann solvers. Modifications are validated using standard shock tube tests. We present results for radiation accretion onto a single black hole, as well as a photon star solution for radiation in unstable hydrostatic equilibrium, demonstrating both collapse and dispersion under perturbations.

entry.title: Variational wavefunctions for ideal anyon gas: superfluid and skyrmion Hall crystal
entry.summary: The ground state of an ideal gas of anyons with statistical angle $θ\in(0,π)$ is a long-standing open problem that has gained renewed relevance with the observation of fractional Chern insulators. We construct variational wavefunctions on the sphere that incorporate the exact anyon statistics, using composite-boson, composite-fermion and parton states as starting points for neural-network optimization. For both spinless and SU(2) semions, independent constructions support a paired anyon superfluid whose energy lies well below that of the best crystal states. Liquids and crystals compete more closely for spinless anyons at $θ=π/3$. For $θ=π/3$ anyons with SU(3) flavor, we identify two competing candidates: a skyrmion Hall crystal, whose pinned flavor texture gives an integer Hall response of the anyons, and a chiral color superconductor of six-anyon clusters. This competition offers a possible explanation for the adjacent reentrant integer quantum anomalous Hall and superconducting phases in twisted MoTe$_2$. In this setting, the color superconductor has $f+if$ symmetry but differs from its BCS counterpart by 3 in chiral central charge. We also provide parameter-free analytical wavefunctions for the color-superconductor ansatz, which reach energies comparable to, or even lower than, those of the best optimized states for SU(3) anyons at $θ=π/3$ and for SU(2) semions.

entry.title: The Gribov problem on the horizon: A short guide to the Gribov-Zwanziger framework and its refinement
entry.summary: Gauge fixing in Yang-Mills theories encounters a non-perturbative obstruction: distinct gauge-equivalent configurations can satisfy the same gauge condition. These are the so-called Gribov copies and their existence challenges the global validity of the Faddeev-Popov prescription. Addressing this ambiguity motivates a framework that connects the geometry of gauge-field space to infrared dynamics. This mini-review introduces the Gribov problem in Euclidean Yang-Mills theories and traces the construction of the Gribov-Zwanziger action and its refinement through the introduction of dimension-two condensates. We discuss the resulting infrared propagators, their comparison to lattice results, and the role of BRST symmetry, before surveying selected applications and open questions.

entry.title: Model-independent Constraints on Dark Energy Density from CMB-SPA, DESI DR2 BAO, and Updated Type Ia Supernova Compilations
entry.summary: Recent combinations of DESI BAO, CMB, and Type~Ia supernova data report a preference for evolving dark energy that is obtained within the $(w_0, w_a)$ parameterization and depends on the choice of SN~Ia compilation. We constrain the dark energy density ratio $X(z) \equiv ρ_{\rm DE}(z)/ρ_{\rm DE}(0)$ at five redshifts over $0 < z < 2.33$, without assuming a parametric form for the equation of state, using CMB data from SPT-3G, Planck~2018, and ACT~DR6 (hereafter CMB-SPA), DESI~DR2 BAO, and the updated Pantheon+, Union3.1, and DES-Dovekie SN~Ia compilations. For all three compilations, $X(z)$ rises above unity at low redshift, crosses unity near $z \approx 1$, and falls below unity at higher redshift. Depending on the SN~Ia compilation, the preference for a departure from a cosmological constant is $2.3$--$2.8σ$ with the five $X(z)$ knots, compared with $3.0$--$3.2σ$ in the $(w_0, w_a)$ parameterization. Because $X(z)$ is constrained locally in redshift, we can trace how the $Λ$CDM tension between each pair of probes propagates into its shape. The tension between BAO and the CMB in the $h r_d$--$Ω_m$ plane reproduces this "see-saw" shape, whereas the $Ω_m$ tension between SNe~Ia and the CMB only raises $X(z)$ slightly and nearly uniformly. The origin of the BAO--CMB tension can be tested by Euclid and Roman BAO measurements at $z \gtrsim 1$. We derive the distance prior $(R, \ell_A, ω_b)$ from CMB-SPA data and show that it retains essentially all the information on $X(z)$ in the CMB-SPA power spectra without the lensing reconstruction, and that adding the lensing reconstruction only marginally increases the information on dark energy. Our work demonstrates the importance of model independence in exploring the nature of dark energy.

entry.title: First Post-Newtonian Cross Terms in Hierarchical Triple Systems: Multiple-Scale Averaging and its Canonical Consistency
entry.summary: We develop a two-stage multiple-scale method for hierarchical triple systems, using osculating orbital elements and time as the independent variable. We examine the disputed cross terms at orders $δ\varepsilon^{3/2}$ and $δ\varepsilon^{7/2}$, for which the multiple-scale results of Lim and Rodriguez (LR) disagree with the effective field theory results of Kuntz, Serra, and Trincherini (KST). Here, $δ$ is the first post-Newtonian (1PN) parameter, and $\varepsilon=a_*/a_2$ ($a_*\simeq a_1$) measures the orbital hierarchy. These terms arise from couplings between relativistic interactions and the tidal field of the third body. Our results agree with KST: there is no secular term at order $δ\varepsilon^{3/2}$, while the $δ\varepsilon^{7/2}$ contribution consists of three parts: a direct term, a first-stage coupling between the inner binary's center-of-mass motion and the tidal field, and a second-stage coupling between the 1PN dipole and the quadrupole. Their sum reproduces the inner-orbit secular dynamics generated by KST's magnetic 1PN--quadrupole Hamiltonian, including its exact mass dependence, for nonsingular eccentricities and inclinations in the nonresonant, hierarchical weak-field regime. The analysis includes mean-anomaly perturbations and resubstitution of short-period corrections in both directions. We clarify how the choice of averaging variable affects the normalization of the mean elements and establish agreement with canonical perturbation theory. In particular, osculating and canonical mean elements give the same inner-orbit secular rates at this order.

entry.title: Quantum Open Effective Field Theory: anomalous decoherence
entry.summary: We study decoherence of a scalar field coupled to ``anomalous'' environments with critical behavior with the Schwinger-Keldysh including the influence functional, and the quantum master equation (QME) up to second order in the coupling. The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation yields a Langevin equation and the Lindblad (QME) includes \emph{time dependent rates} allowing to study transient dynamics. We focus on three examples featuring non-Markov dynamics that cannot be described with S-matrix/Fermi's golden rule rates \textbf{i) Unparticle physics:} a conformal sector beyond the Standard Model at an infrared fixed point featuring correlation functions with anomalous scaling dimensions, \textbf{ii) Threshold and infrared enhancement:} when the mass shell of the field coincides with or is near to a kinematic threshold of the spectral density of the bath, \textbf{iii) Critical environments:} the bath is at a critical point, correlation functions scale with anomalous dimensions and long-wavelength fluctuations feature critical slowing down. In all cases the reduced density matrix undergoes decoherence in the energy basis of the probe, and off-diagonal matrix elements decay as $e^{-Φ(t)}$ with $Φ(t)>0 $ the \emph{decoherence function} and $Γ(t) = \dotΦ(t)$ the decoherence rate. In all cases we find that either transient or asymptotically $Φ(t) \propto t^{-μ}~;~ μ>0$ with $μ$, determined by the behavior of the spectral density at threshold and the anomalous scaling dimensions of the correlation functions, or $Φ(t) \propto \ln(t)$ for the infrared case. For a critical environment there is a new dynamical scaling exponent. A probe of frequency $ω_q$ is resonant with a \emph{critically slow} quasiparticle for $q_*\propto ω^{1/z}_q$ at which decoherence is strongly \emph{enhanced}.

entry.title: Post-Newtonian Secular Dynamics of Hierarchical Triple Systems: A Consistent Canonical Treatment of Cross Terms
entry.summary: We derive the secular Hamiltonian for hierarchical triple systems from the Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) three-body Hamiltonian through first post-Newtonian (1PN) order, using Lie--Hori--Deprit canonical perturbation theory and time averaging over the inner and outer orbits. The canonical framework systematically incorporates higher-order cross terms through scalar generating functions and Poisson brackets while preserving the Hamiltonian structure. We recover the electric and magnetic 1PN--quadrupole terms of Kuntz, Serra, and Trincherini (KST), rather than those reported by Lim and Rodriguez (LR). We further derive the next-to-leading-order 1PN--quadrupole term, the Newtonian quadrupole-squared Hamiltonian, and a third-order coupling between inner 1PN precession and the squared quadrupole. The outer-pericenter dependence of the quadrupole-squared Hamiltonian is removable by a canonical redefinition of the mean elements. Direct integrations of the Einstein--Infeld--Hoffmann (EIH) equations confirm the de Sitter term, the direct electric term, and the binding-energy renormalization of the inner-binary mass. For the systems considered by LR, the canonical terms do not reproduce the extreme merger acceleration they reported. Instead, the relativistic modulation of the eccentricity cycles is driven primarily by the outer-pericenter-dependent part of the next-to-leading-order 1PN--quadrupole term.

entry.title: On the nature of low-energy electronic states in twisted bilayer graphene: a first-principles study
entry.summary: The nature of low-energy electronic states in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) near the magic angle has been extensively discussed in the literature on qualitative grounds, since these states play a key role in the construction of effective few-band models toward a many-body theory. Here, we report extensive and systematic first-principles calculations of TBG electronic states in the magic-angle range, using density functional theory with no further approximations. We construct moiré-scale localized Wannier states for the low-energy bands and develop an effective ten-band model for each $K$ valley. The Wannier orbitals contain both atomic and moiré-scale details and are centered near the high-symmetry stackings in the moiré cell. We calculate Coulomb and exchange integrals of these localized states, quantities that are the basic ingredients in many-body models. We also compare the values of these integrals to those obtained or assumed in previous works. By symmetrizing the ten-band Hamiltonians and basis orbitals, we provide insight into how the dominant hoppings between the flat-band orbitals evolve as a function of twist angle.

entry.title: Stealth scalars on prescribed dark-energy backgrounds: reconstruction, branch regularity, and perturbative bounds
entry.summary: We reconstruct homogeneous stealth scalar fields on prescribed Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker backgrounds with constant or evolving dark-energy equations of state. The scalar stress tensor vanishes, so the expansion history is supported by an independent background sector. Eliminating the self-interaction potential yields a Riccati equation for the scalar profile. We use it to distinguish exact stealthness from global regularity and from the stronger identification of a term in the scalar stress tensor with the prescribed dark-energy density. We prove that this sector-preserving identification is not dynamically invariant in a mixed flat constant-$w$ cosmology. For radiation-free $w$CDM backgrounds, a hypergeometric representation allows the regular and singular branches to be separated by a background-dependent threshold. At conformal coupling the reconstruction instead reduces to an exact comoving-distance quadrature, valid for arbitrary regular flat histories, including radiation. A CPL phantom-divide crossing does not singularize the background stealth equation, although the perturbations of the prescribed dark-energy sector require an independent treatment. The scalar--tensor description gives luminal high-frequency propagation under a positive effective Planck mass. If the field tracks its cosmological value locally without screening, Cassini constraints strongly suppress the corresponding late-time gravitational responses.

entry.title: FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge: Dataset and Cosmological Inference Competition
entry.summary: Weak gravitational lensing is a powerful cosmological probe that enables direct mapping of the matter distribution and precise constraints on the fundamental parameters governing structure formation in the universe. In recent years, machine learning has shown strong potential for extracting cosmological information from weak-lensing data beyond traditional summary statistics. However, progress has been limited by the lack of standardized benchmarks that capture the complexity of the dataset, simulator imperfections, and various systematic biases encountered in realistic analyses. To address this gap, we present the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing Machine Learning Uncertainty Challenge, one of the NeurIPS 2025 competitions, as a benchmark dataset and evaluation study. Our dataset reflects realistic weak-lensing observations, incorporating multiple systematic biases, and thereby providing a controlled testbed for robust cosmological inference under uncertainties. We summarize the main methodological advances developed by the winners of our challenge, including data augmentation with conditional optimal transport, an AI-agent-driven approach for parameter inference, ensemble learning, Vision Transformer-based architectures, and physics-informed feature integration. By unifying the benchmark dataset and the winning solutions, this work provides a community resource for developing and evaluating machine learning methods for weak lensing cosmology and, more broadly, for scientific inference under systematic uncertainties.

entry.title: A panchromatic photometric and spectroscopic modeling of SN1987A from 200 to 800d
entry.summary: Type II supernovae (SNe) at 1-3yr after explosion can document not only the preSN mass loss history of massive stars but also the chemistry of the inner ejecta rich in metals and eventually molecules and dust. With the aim of modeling SN1987A, we present a grid of radiative-transfer models of Type II SNe at Zsun/3, covering an initial mass range between 11 and 21Msun, a fixed ejecta kinetic energy of 1.2e51erg, and ~0.08Msun of 56Ni. The influence of metallicity at such late times is found to be relatively weak. In this model set, the [OI]6330A flux at 1-2yr varies non-monotonically with Minit. It first rises with Minit due to the growing O abundance but drops for M>17-19Msun due to the higher ejecta density, with little change to the rest of the optical spectrum. Assuming CO molecules account for 90% of the cooling in the C/O shell leads to a 10-20% reduction in the [OI] flux, equivalent to an O(1Msun) reduction in Minit at M<19Msun. The fractional [OI] flux rises from 200 to ~600d but decreases beyond. We obtain a good agreement to SN1987A for all Minit apart from [OI], which appears in the optical as the only discriminant between models. The 13Msun model yields the best match, from UV to IR, but a higher Minit may result with allowance for strong CO and SiO cooling. Past 500d, a growing amount of dust below ~2000km/s is essential to account for the ~1.5mag optical excess fading relative to predictions from decay power. Adopting 0.1mic silicate grains, we find a dust mass of 1e-4Msun at 600d rising to a few 1e-3Msun at 700-800d. We also found that the 200-800d International Ultraviolet Explorer spectra of SN1987A are all contaminated by a background hot star, which also causes the relative UV brightening past 500d. Such contamination may complicate the interpretation of more distant SNe II at >~2yr once or if they fade to O(1e5Lsun) [abridged].

entry.title: Eccentric Stellar-mass Binary Black Holes: Population, Detectability, and Waveform Analysis in the LISA and LIGO Era
entry.summary: Eccentric binary black holes (BBHs) formed through dynamical interactions can significantly contribute to gravitational wave (GW) detections. In this work, we present a simulated catalog of dynamically-formed, stellar-mass BBHs in the local universe, incorporating contributions from the Galactic field (flyby interactions), Galactic nucleus (eccentric Kozai-Lidov evolution), and globular clusters (N-body interactions). Our results predict a wide, highly eccentric BBH population in the Milky Way (MW), with source counts of $\sim 25, 9, 3, 1, <1$ for a 4-year LISA mission and $\sim 36, 13, 5, 2, 1$ for a 10-year mission, at $\mathrm{SNR} > 1, 3, 8, 20, 50$, respectively. Extending this model to cosmological populations, we show that different dynamical channels can produce distinct eccentricity distributions in the LVK band and can contribute hundreds of additional low-SNR mHz sources. Specifically, our model yields a merger rate of $Γ\sim 9 \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and $\sim 150$ extragalactic mHz BBHs with $\mathrm{SNR} > 1$. However, due to the lower mass and weaker GW signals of stellar-mass BBHs, this number declines sharply at higher detection thresholds (e.g., $\sim 1$ for $\mathrm{SNR} > 8$). We further highlight the impact of eccentric BBH signals on the LISA global fit, showing that their individual harmonics can be independently detected in the Milky Way, and may mimic circular binaries with systematically biased chirp masses. Lastly, we show that post-Newtonian waveforms converge reliably for eccentric BBHs with masses of $\lesssim 10^3 M_\odot$ in the mHz band. Overall, eccentric BBHs represent a prevalent and promising target for future space-based GW observatories. The simulated catalog and the LISA Eccentricity Astrophysics Package (LEAP) developed in this work are publicly available at https://github.com/zeyuanxuan/lisa-leap/.

entry.title: Analysis of Quartic Potential Problems Using Fredholm Integral Operators with Airy Functions
entry.summary: Fredholm integral operators that commute with the Hamiltonians of certain quantum mechanical systems with quartic potentials are introduced in closed analytical form. The operators are expressed in terms of the Airy function, and their eigenvalues fall off exponentially. Using these operators we obtain an exact dual description in terms of infinite one-dimensional chains. The systems discussed include the anharmonic quartic oscillator as well as multivariable potentials and higher dimensional systems. We compute a few moments of the Fredholm operators, using matrix models in the higher dimensional case, and we show how those can be used to approximate the energy spectrum and obtain estimates of the asymptotic behavior of the wavefunctions.

entry.title: Topology of the Fermi surface and universality of the metal-metal and metal-insulator transitions: $d$-dimensional Hatsugai-Kohmoto model as an example
entry.summary: The earlier theory \cite{Chitov:2025} of the quantum phase transitions related to the change of the Fermi Surface Topology (FST) is advanced. For such transitions the Fermi surface as a quantum critical manifold determined by the Lee-Yang zeros, the order parameter $\mathcal{P}$ as the $d$-volume of the Fermi sea, and the special FST universality class were introduced in \cite{Chitov:2025}. The exactly solvable Hatsugai-Kohmoto (HK) $d$-dimensional ($d=1,2,3$) model of interacting fermions is analyzed. We explore the relation between the Lee-Yang zeros, the Luttinger and the plateau (Oshikawa) theorems. The validity of the Luttinger theorem in the HK model is confirmed. It is shown that the order parameter $\mathcal{P}$ and the FST universality class describe the transitions between metal and band/Mott insulators, as well as the Lifshitz and van Hove gapless-to-gapless transitions. The gapless phases are established to be the ferromagnetic Fermi liquids (metals), where the quantum critical manifold is also a locus of ferromagnetic order with spontaneous breaking of the rotational symmetry occurring at $T=0$. In addition to the conventional paradigm with a continuous order parameter, we apply the homology theory to analyze the FST transitions. They are critical points of the Morse function. To quantify FST we use the Euler characteristic, which is calculated for each phase of the HK model. We claim that the FST universality class is robust with respect to interactions and other model details, under the condition that the conduction band function is smooth and the critical points are non-degenerate.

entry.title: Large-D approach to nearly critical holographic matter and Yang-Mills deconfinement
entry.summary: We study a systematic expansion of dynamical black hole solutions in a class of five-dimensional Einstein-dilaton theories that are holographically dual to nearly critical, strongly coupled four-dimensional field theories. The expansion is motivated, through dimensional reduction, by the large-D limit of pure gravity, where D is the number of spacetime dimensions. At leading nontrivial order, the Einstein equations reduce to a closed set of non-relativistic hydrodynamic equations in four dimensions, as first shown in our previous letter; these equations generalize the large-D effective theory of black branes. We derive the thermodynamics and hydrodynamics of the system from black hole thermodynamics and the holographic dictionary, and show that the energy-momentum tensor extracted from the near-boundary geometry is conserved precisely when the effective equations hold. We analyze planar, cylindrical, and spherical domain walls between coexisting phases, as well as non-equilibrium steady-state walls with nonzero momentum flux. We also show how the near-horizon geometry can be completed by a holographic flow to an asymptotically AdS5 region. Finally, as an application to the confinement-deconfinement transition of Yang-Mills theory, we construct the domain wall between the confined and deconfined phases in improved holographic QCD, compute its surface tension, and compare it with recent lattice results.

entry.title: How does geometry shape quantum emission in rotating bumblebee gravity?
entry.summary: We compare propagation and static emission estimates in a rotating metric geometry and a stationary metric-affine bumblebee geometry. Their distinct constructions and spatial asymptotics are kept, and normalized Killing times define the physical frequencies and angular velocities. Direct invariant calculations identify the metric-affine outer root and open exterior axes as curvature singularities for generic rotation. The obstruction at bifurcation surface poles concerns the smoothness of the bumblebee field independently. Its mixed meridional component couples angular channels; finite transverse energy fixes the adopted axial condition and defines a self adjoint stationary operator on bounded exterior annuli. For the metric geometry, we construct normalized radiative scalar modes with specified Unruh data, evaluate the horizon frequency transformation, and include spontaneous superradiant emission through the radial scattering map. We prove positivity of the axisymmetric potential and compute numerical transmission factors and a partial scalar energy spectrum alongside an analytical lower bound. The static emission estimates use the stated Stefan-Boltzmann model.

entry.title: Spin Textures and Eigenstate Evolution of Isospectrally Patterned Lattices
entry.summary: Isospectrally patterned lattices exhibit a composite band structure with a tunable ratio of localized versus delocalized eigenstates that is controlled by the underlying phase gradient. We show that the lattice Hamiltonian can be interpreted as that of a single spin which, exposed to a rotating magnetic field, hops across the lattice with a spin flip. In the low- and high-energy part of the band, the localized states show an envelope of oscillatory character separated by quasi-nodes. Spin peaks occur at the locations of these quasi-nodes and provide a unique spin texture to the eigenstates, which becomes increasingly complex with increasing degree of excitation. The crossover from localization to delocalization and vice versa leaves its fingerprints in the Fourier spectrum of the eigenstates: the original bimodal frequency distribution widens with increasing degree of excitation, moves across the spectral window, and finally culminates in an extremely narrow frequency peak. In the course of this evolution, the spin texture undergoes a rearrangement transition involving different characteristic (ir)regular patterns which we quantify by considering the total variation of the local spin fluctuations. Our results demonstrate the variety of the spectral properties of isospectrally patterned lattices, which holds great prospect, in particular when considering higher lattice or cell dimensions.

entry.title: Current-voltage characteristics of layered cuprate superconductors with intrinsic Josephson junctions
entry.summary: A brief review of the results for the current-voltage characteristics study in highly anisotropic cuprate superconductors is presented, considering the existence of the intrinsic Josephson effect in multilayer HTSC compounds. We analyzed the observations of multi-branch current-voltage characteristics for current in the c-direction both for the hole-doped and electron-doped cuprate SCs wich conveniently viewed as a strack of intrinsic Josephson junctions, where the CuO2 layers serve as superconducting plates and the buffer layers as dielectric interlayers. It was shown that the tunneling characteristics of intrinsic Josephson junctions in optimally doped p- and n-type cuprates indicate a predominantly d-wave symmetry of the order parameter, demonstrating high conductivity in the subgap regime: U < 2delta/e. The analysis carried out confirms the theoretically predicted power-law dependences U ~ I^gamma with gamma = (0.33 - 0.50) in the hole-doped Bi- and Tl-compounds, which is typical for SCs with monotonic dx^2-y^2 - wave symmetry of the order parameter and with gamma = (0.70 - 0.76) for electron-doped SCs with a non-monotonic d-wave symmetry within the framework of the two-band/two-gap model.

entry.title: Krylov complexity and spectral density of BMN matrix model
entry.summary: We use Krylov complexity as a typical diagnostic of quantum many body dynamics in the context of BMN matrix model at large mass gap. We calculate several physical entities, for example, the moments and return amplitudes at large mass deformation. We calculate them for both spread complexity of states as well as Krylov growth of operators in the matrix model. We propose a general expression for the moments at any given order $n$. We also discuss orthogonal polynomials for spread as well as operator Krylov complexity. In the context of the Krylov operator growth we further compute the spectral function and the density of states. A careful analysis of the spectral function near the resonance reveals various IR divergences in addition to the physical collective modes. These collective modes appear to be exceptionally stable due to large mass gap. On the other hand, the UV of the theory appears to be extremely damped due to higher scattering rates. We carefully diagnose these IR divergences near resonance which reveals that these collective modes are in fact non-propagating and should be thought of as diffusion modes or relaxation modes with infinite relaxation time. We also calculate the Krylov variance and Krylov entropy for the matrix model and in particular at early time. The linear early time growth of the Krylov entropy confirms the onset of quantum chaos in the matrix model at large mass gap.

entry.title: Perturbative Coulomb branches on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$: the global D-term potential
entry.summary: We develop a Wilsonian description of perturbative D-terms in 4d $\mathcal N=1$ gauge theories on $\mathbb R^3\times S^1$ with chiral Kaluza--Klein spectra. A closed-form, one-loop-exact coefficient of the auxiliary D fields, including 4d Fayet--Iliopoulos parameters and globally valid throughout the holonomy space, determines the leading holonomy potential away from massless thresholds. We establish uniform weak-coupling control there and match across thresholds by retaining the light fields. Gauge-anomaly cancellation renders the Coulomb-slice vacuum equations affine within each chamber bounded by the thresholds, enabling exact linear analysis of their zero sets and numerical reconstruction through DBSCAN clustering of approximate zeros, LPCA denoising, and RANSAC hyperplane detection. Complementing the rank-one applications of the accompanying Letter, we study flavor-twist dependence in the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ $\mathcal N=4$ theory, and illustrate the numerical reconstruction in higher-rank R-twisted Argyres--Douglas reductions of interest in the SCFT/VOA correspondence. We also relate the same D-term data to leading stationary-phase equations of supersymmetric partition functions and a decompactification limit of the torus twisted superpotential.
